apps.localizedDescription:
CyPort contains no game files. You need your own legally bought copy of Cyberpunk 2077 for Mac (GOG, version 2.3.1). The app is built on your Mac from that copy. CyPort is an independent fan project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by CD PROJEKT RED. Cyberpunk 2077 is a trademark of CD PROJEKT S.A.

Status:

Tested on: iPhone 16 Pro Max (A18 Pro, 8 GB), iOS 27.0.1, built with Xcode 27.

versions.localizedDescription:
CyPort v1.3:

Run your own copy of Cyberpunk 2077 for Mac natively on iPhone and iPad – no emulation, no streaming.

Not affiliated with CD PROJEKT RED.

This release is about frame rate, smoothness and controllers.

🖥️ 120 Hz:

• iOS keeps a game's screen at 60 Hz unless the app asks for more, and the Mac game never asks. So VSync 40 showed as 30, and 120 / Off stopped at 60.
• CyPort now switches the screen to 120 Hz whenever the game's frame cap needs it (VSync 40, 120 or Off), and back to normal for 30 / 60 to save battery. Menus now run at 120 FPS with VSync 120.

🎞️ Smooth frame pacing (start screen, on by default):

• When the phone can't keep up with the cap (e.g. VSync 120 but the phone manages 75), frames alternate between 17 and 25 ms – the FPS counter looks fine, but it feels choppy.
• CyPort now holds the highest even rate the phone really keeps up with – 120, 60, 40 or 30 FPS, never above your in-game setting – and now and then tries the next step up. The FPS overlay shows actual/target.

⚡ Low-latency input (start screen, off by default):

• Controls react about a frame sooner: the game reads input only when at most one frame is still on the GPU.
• The earlier version of this used 2 frame buffers, which halved the frame rate (120 → 60, 60 → 30). That is gone.

🎮 Controller fixes:

• Third-party controllers (EasySMX, 8BitDo, generic "HID" / MFi) are shown to the game as an Xbox controller – the game only knows Xbox, DualSense and DualShock 4, and often ignored others.
• A controller that is already connected when the game starts now works right away (before, it did nothing at "press space to continue" until it was unplugged and plugged in again).
• When a controller connects, the on-screen pad is withdrawn first, so the game always makes the real one active.
• A Bluetooth controller that drops out for a second no longer brings the on-screen pad back.

Also:

• TV out now shows the picture on the phone too, and the screen no longer dims while playing.
• The start screen's switches can't be cut off any more.

Performance tips:

• Resolution 1434 × 660 on the start screen.
• VSync 40 for the open world: smooth on the 120 Hz screen and something the phone can hold. 60–120 for menus and short sessions – higher caps make the phone hot faster.
• Leave frame generation off. A clip-on phone cooler helps more than any setting.

Upgrading:

Rebuild the IPA with this version (./build.sh or Build CyPort.command, see the README), then reinstall. Your game data, saves and settings stay in place.

Known issues:

• The phone still throttles in long open-world sessions; expect ~25–30 FPS while driving once it's hot.
• Smooth frame pacing and low-latency input v2 are new and not yet tested in a full play session – please report stutter or wrong frame rates (the log says smooth pacing: / frame pacing: at each change).
